candidates.title: Anne Imhof: House of Swans
candidates.blurb: Imhof's first Asia institutional solo adapts her durational performance language to Tai Kwun's former prison architecture.

candidates.title: Treasures of Global Jewellery from The Metropolitan Museum of Art: The Body Transformed
candidates.blurb: Met jewellery survey tracking how adornment shaped identity across cultures, a rare loan bringing New York's holdings to Asia.

candidates.title: Ancient Egypt Unveiled: Treasures from Egyptian Museums
candidates.blurb: Direct loans from Egyptian state collections, positioning HKPM as a Belt and Road cultural hub beyond its Qing remit.

candidates.title: The Hong Kong Jockey Club Series: Treasures of the Mughal Court from the Victoria and Albert Museum
candidates.blurb: V&A Mughal holdings tour Hong Kong, extending the museum's imperial-crossover thesis from Qing-Versailles to Indo-Persian courts.

candidates.title: Alicja Kwade: Waiting Pavilions
candidates.blurb: Kwade's mirrored structures occupy Tai Kwun's open-air prison yard, literalising detention as suspended time.

candidates.title: Fermata: Hong Kong in Venice
candidates.blurb: The 61st Venice Biennale collateral returns home, testing whether Hong Kong's official pavilion has local resonance after the international run.

candidates.title: Live: Hong Kong Art Exhibition
candidates.blurb: Broad-spectrum survey of Hong Kong contemporary practice, a rare institutional stocktake of the city's living artists.

candidates.title: Proudly from Canton: The Muwen Tang Collection of Cantonese and Export Art
candidates.blurb: Private collection of Cantonese export ware—porcelain, paintings—surfaces Hong Kong's Pearl River Delta trade genealogy.

candidates.title: A History of China in Silk: The Chris Hall Collection at the Hong Kong Palace Museum
candidates.blurb: Chris Hall's textile archive maps Chinese silk production across dynasties, tracing aesthetic and technical lineages.

candidates.title: Joyful Encounters: The Connoisseurship and Art of Wong Kwan Shut
candidates.blurb: Scholar-artist Wong Kwan Shut's collection and practice examined, reviving the literati tradition through a 20th-century Hong Kong lens.

candidates.title: The Hong Kong Jockey Club Series: A Day in the City — An Experimental Study of Things Across Time
candidates.blurb: Object-based study of urban daily life across historical epochs, positioning material culture as ethnographic archive.

candidates.title: Heavenly Horses: Masterpieces from the Palace Museum
candidates.blurb: Equestrian art from Beijing's Palace Museum, tracing the horse as military, diplomatic, and aesthetic motif in Chinese painting.

candidates.title: The Hong Kong Jockey Club Series: The Art of Armaments — Qing Dynasty Military Collection from The Palace Museum
candidates.blurb: Qing weaponry as decorative art, examining how imperial martial culture aestheticised violence through craftsmanship.
candidates.why_shortlisted: Material culture, aesthetic reading of power
